title: Florida man indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting on ransomware data-recovery firm
date_note: 404 Media (published Nov 19) says the indictment was filed on Wednesday, i.e. Nov 18; the exact filing date is not stated.
summary: 404 Media reports that Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar was indicted in the District of Rhode Island on three counts of wire fraud. Prosecutors allege his Florida ransomware data-recovery company claimed advanced tools but instead bought decryption keys from the gangs and overcharged clients. FBI agents posed as a ransomware victim and as the attackers in a sting.
plain: A company that promised to recover data after ransomware allegedly just paid the criminals and marked up the price. The FBI caught it with a staged attack.
exec: Recovery firms that quietly pay ransoms can overcharge victims; vet them before hiring in a crisis.
action: Before hiring a ransomware recovery firm, ask in writing whether it will pay the attackers and how it prices that, and report fraud to the FBI.
impact: Per 404 Media's account of the indictment, a Kansas business was allegedly charged $720,000 and the firm allegedly paid a gang about $445,000 in bitcoin.
